articles.body:
CORAL GABLES, Fla. — Inside the University of Miami's presidential conference room, on giant television monitors against the far wall, CNBC's afternoon program projects a dismal day.

The latest stock market numbers crawl across the bottom of the screen — a reminder to Joe Echevarria, the school's president, of his past life as a business executive for the world's largest professional services and accounting firm, Deloitte.

"You see that ticker thing?" he points toward the screen. "We used to get pounded by shareholders. Every. Single. Day. Now, we lose a football game and it's bad. But that world prepared me for this one."

In a dark, slimly fitted suit, peering through black spectacles and moving with the suave befitting of the U itself, Echevarria (pronounced ehchuh-vah-reeuh) makes no apologies for his present position: The University of Miami refuses to accept the current status quo as a member of the second class in the growing caste system within college athletics.

And if anyone questions him, Echevarria has a simple retort: It's just business .

"We are proud members of the ACC. If the economics were even, we wouldn't be having any of these conversations," he told Yahoo Sports in an interview this week. "Thing is, we sit in the second tier. It's a reason we don't get a vote on the 24-team playoff and the Big Ten and SEC do."

A calculated businessman, Echevarria presides over one of the country's most attractive private universities (18% acceptance rate), with a burgeoning healthcare system that he helped resurrect years ago ($5.2 billion in revenue), a research department that carries the highest designation available (R1), and a member in one of the most exclusive clubs in higher education, the Association of American Universities (AAU).

Oh, and a football program — the essential brand of the university — that has roared back to life under coach Mario Cristobal and, coincidentally, on this particular week, is ranked No. 1 in the nation for the first time in nearly a quarter of a century.

The buzz across campus over the top billing — a fleeting and inconsequential numerical figure, Echevarria acknowledges — is emblematic of the football program's brand. He describes it as "outsized."

"I recently hired a world-class scientist, a luminary and no one is asking me anything. He's No. 1 in the world! Zero talk!" the president says, bellowing with laughter. "We get to No. 1 for one week and we're back and the greatest!"

Echevarria taps the pin affixed to his suit jacket's lapel: Miami's iconic, two-toned 'U' logo that, while representative of this place as a whole, is most recognizable because of the football program's famed helmets.

This , he says, is why Miami is now positioning itself for a move into college athletics's top financial and social stratosphere, the SEC and Big Ten; why the school (and several others in the ACC) has been forced to explore aspects of football independence; and why the university, despite rebuke from congressional lawmakers and those connected to the White House, is fighting against a federal bill that stands to prevent further realignment in the industry.

"You cannot lock us into a conference," he says, flatly.

"The fact is that we won about every game you could win last year and maxed out in revenue in our current [ACC] sharing model. And we made the same amount of money as other institutions [in the Big Ten and SEC] whose football programs operate at different levels of investment and performance."

If projections are accurate, Echevarria says, the Big Ten and SEC, already distributing an average of $25 million more to each of their schools than the ACC, will almost double their edge when they renegotiate their television contracts in 2030 — the year that the SEC may execute a look-in clause with ESPN and when the Big Ten's current media rights deal expires.

The ACC's binding television contract with ESPN doesn't end until 2036, and though the league pushed through an uneven revenue distribution model, the financial inequities with the power two leagues is fixed — still very much a frustrating point for administrators like Echevarria.

The financial gap has materialized into on-field, on-court success as well as viewership ratings and, perhaps most concerning for him, governing authority.

Over the last two academic years — since the two behemoths expanded to further consolidate college football's biggest brands — the SEC and Big Ten have been responsible for 63% of College Football Playoff participants, 66% of Sweet 16 teams and at least 85% of the top-10 most-watched regular season college football games. Two-and-a-half years ago, as the two conferences threatened to start their own football postseason, the other leagues granted them authority on future format — something that, this very week, they used to expand to a 24-team field starting next year, agreeing to a new contract of more than $1.6 billion annually with ESPN instead of testing the open market.

"There's a reason certain conferences and programs have a greater influence in shaping the future of college football," Echevarria says. "Their collective competitive success and viewership give them leverage. There's no secret to this. It's just business."

Miami, as well as other ACC programs, have accelerated their exploration into future conference membership. But the reasons go beyond the financial, athletic, viewership and governance differences mentioned above.

How independence, Amazon could factor in

A bill working its way through Congress, the Protect College Sports Act, features a provision that caps power league membership at 20 schools and requires a university moving within power conferences to operate as an independent for three years before joining a new league. The concept has divided the ACC, with 13 members fully behind the legislation and four against it.

It's made for some awkwardness. ACC commissioner Jim Phillips and the league office is in an "impossible position," quipped one person familiar with the matter. "He's trying to make the best of it."

Presidents at Miami, Florida State, Clemson and North Carolina signed a letter encouraging leaders in the House of Representatives to increase the power conference cap to 22 teams and to eliminate the independent probationary period. It would pave an easier path for the aspiring schools to join the Big Ten, currently at 18 members, or the SEC, currently at 16.

The provision is an "unfair advantage" that "no modern enterprise" would dare accept, Echevarria says. "It's illogical."

Others see it differently. The provision, Section 205 of the bill, is intended to prevent the SEC and Big Ten from "joining forces to create a super league," bill author Sen. Ted Cruz says.

But in a recent interview with Tomahawk Nation, Florida State board chairman Peter Collins, leading the Seminoles' efforts against this provision in the bill, says the concept "effectively eliminates our [expansion] options that we just fought for" with the ACC. The settlement of a lawsuit filed by FSU and Clemson against the ACC resulted in more palatable exit fees for those wanting to leave the conference.

By 2030 — there's that year again — the fees drop below $100 million per school.

Section 205 has expedited realignment conversations among the schools, many of whom — including Miami — have been exploring life as football independents with possible media entities such as Amazon, those with knowledge of the talks tell Yahoo Sports.

While Echevarria did not disclose details or even acknowledge those conversations, he said that the bill passing Congress would "force us to do it."

"If we have to go independent, I like our chances because we are a national brand," he says. "I wouldn't like to do that because scheduling [other sports] is really tough. It's great for football but what about track, volleyball and the golf team?"

He "hopes that reasonable minds prevail" and House members amend language in the provision. The House is scheduled to return to session in mid-November, where lawmakers are expected to examine the bill, which passed the U.S. Senate last month with a sweeping majority of 77 votes . Any amended bill must be re-adopted by the Senate, a potentially lengthy process that may serve as a death knell for the legislation.

In the meantime, Echevarria and the Hurricanes are preparing for what may be next.

"As an AAU research institution, we line up with the Big Ten's profile," he says, in a jarring comment from a prominent executive about potential membership in another conference. "We have an exceptionally strong profile that compares favorably with leading research institutions across the country. On the geography idea, we line up better with the SEC."

While leaders at the SEC and Big Ten have shown little to no signs publicly that they are willing or plan to expand in the immediate future, expansion moves traditionally unfold under the cloak of darkness.

However, the Big Ten already finds itself stretched east to west across three timezones. Is it worth a dip into the south to further exacerbate travel expenses? It is true that the conference and its television partner, Fox, have shown more aggression in expansion, and the league may benefit from adding bigger brands, such as Miami, to increase the value of its regular season schedule?

In the SEC, expansion conversations among executives — not at all formal — have often centered around other schools outside of the state of Florida. North Carolina and Virginia provide the league with a presence in two new states, high achieving academic brands and strong basketball programs.

Within the league, Florida and South Carolina stand as threats to any addition of other in-state programs such as FSU, Miami or Clemson. A similar situation unfolded years ago with Texas A&M. The Aggies privately objected to the SEC's pursuit of Texas.

One thing, though, is quite clear: Miami is investing millions in its football program and has a roster that many believe exceeds $40 million, topping not only schools in the ACC but many of those in the SEC and Big Ten.

While also managing the academic and research components of the university, Echevarria sits as the top decision-maker on many football-related financial decisions, including the millions approved from donor and sponsor assets to the football program. Echevarria and his executive vice president, Rudy Fernandez, hold daily conversations with athletics personnel about operations and roster spend.

As a Miami graduate, Echevarria saw the rise of Hurricanes football, from after-thought in the 1970s to five national championships in an 18-season span starting in 1983.

"He is very involved," says one person of the president, "like an NFL franchise owner."

And why shouldn't he be? The program costs hundreds of millions of dollars to fund and its success shapes the national narrative of his university. It's why Echevarria isn't afraid to say the quiet part aloud. When Miami joined the ACC in 2004, the landscape was drastically different.

"The next time all these contracts come up, we'll have to revisit that decision," he says. "Does it still make sense or not?"

Echevarria says it's "evident" by the split within the ACC room over the congressional bill — 13 vs. 4 — that not all universities hold intentions of investing to compete with the football powers in the SEC and Big Ten. And that's fine. Those schools have "their own objectives," he said. Those choosing to invest and compete at a high level in football will "search for a place to do that."

Considering the continued growth in the financial gaps between the SEC/Big Ten and everybody else, can Miami afford to wait until the expiration of the ACC's contract a decade from now to make its big move?

Echevarria crosses his legs, leans back in his chair and his eyes dart toward the CNBC stock market ticker running across the screens before him.

"If you're not going to be great at something," he says, "you shouldn't be in it."

articles.title: Millones a la vista
articles.standfirst: El Liverpool dispuesto a ejecutar la opción de compra de Araujo si sigue con este rendimiento
articles.summary: El Liverpool dispuesto a ejecutar la opción de compra de Araujo si sigue con este rendimiento
articles.body: El Liverpool se está cargando de razones para seguir mirando a Ronald Araujo con optimismo. Y preparando la cartera porque deberá desembolsar 55 millones de euros el próximo verano si decide ejecutar la opción de compra pactada para quedarse en propiedad con el defensa uruguayo, cuya adaptación al equipo está superando las expectativas. Su rendimiento, además, ha abierto un escenario que hace unos meses parecía más difícil de imaginar: que Anfield se convierta en el lugar donde el central encuentre la continuidad y el protagonismo que necesitaba. Araujo ha caído de pie. Recolocado como lateral, está respondiendo con solvencia a una función que exige recorrido, disciplina táctica y capacidad para interpretar diferentes situaciones del juego. Su fortaleza física y su agresividad defensiva le permiten competir en la banda, mientras que su presencia en ataque ha añadido otro argumento que ya demostró en el Barça: los goles. El uruguayo no solo está cumpliendo, sino que está demostrando que puede ofrecer soluciones en más de una posición. Andoni Iraola conoce bien las virtudes del futbolista y ha encontrado la manera de aprovecharlas. "Ronald necesitaba este cambio y ha llegado con humildad; es un jugador experimentado de un club grande, preparado para jugar en diferentes posiciones", explicó el técnico, convencido de que la versatilidad del defensa es una herramienta valiosa para el equipo. El propio Araujo, por su parte, ha dejado claro que ahora mismo su prioridad es jugar y sentirse importante. "Creo que aquí estoy encontrando lo que necesitaba, que era jugar, sentirme importante y mostrar mi fútbol. Es muy pronto para hablar de estas cosas. Estoy teniendo minutos de juego, que es lo que quiero y luego veremos qué pasa en el futuro", señaló. Sus palabras invitan a la prudencia. El futbolista no quiere precipitar acontecimientos y el Liverpool todavía deberá valorar si la inversión merece la pena. 55 millones no son una cifra menor, ni siquiera para un club de la dimensión de los ‘reds’. Pero el rendimiento del uruguayo está alimentando el debate y reforzando su candidatura a continuar. El Barcelona, mientras, se frota las manos ante esta cantidad de dinero que le puede caer en el próximo mercado estival. Un dinero que puede utilizar en la contratación de un defensa experimentado que dé solvencia a una línea defensiva muy joven que necesita futbolistas ya curtidos en grandes partidos europeos. El próximo verano llegará la hora de tomar una decisión. Hasta entonces, Araujo tiene una misión clara: seguir convenciendo sobre el césped. Cada partido, cada actuación y cada gol pueden acercarle a un futuro definitivo en Liverpool. Los millones ya están sobre la mesa; ahora, el fútbol tendrá la última palabra.

articles.title: El Liverpool chequea la cesión de Elliott en Valencia
articles.standfirst: Kiko Espinar, scout de los 'reds' es España hace una visita al jugador, a Braulio y a Aguirre en la ciudad deportiva
articles.summary: Kiko Espinar, scout de los 'reds' es España hace una visita al jugador, a Braulio y a Aguirre en la ciudad deportiva
articles.body: ¿Cómo le va a Harvey Elliott en el Valencia? El Liverpool ha querido chequear la cesión de una de sus perlas de la cantera en España. El atacante está jugando poco, incluso se le ha puesto un nutricionista para que recupere el peso y la forma. Poco a poco debe ir entrando porque se trata de un jugador de máxima calidad, pero para ello es clave que vuelva a ser competitivo tras estar demasiado tiempo parado. Durante la mañana de hoy, Braulio Vázquez, director deportivo del club de Mestalla, ha recibido la visita de Kiko Espinar, uno de los hombres fuertes del Liverpool en España. En la reunión se ha descartado la posibilidad de que el jugador regrese a Inglaterra rompiendo la cesión en el mes de enero. El ojeador del equipo Premier ha hablado también con Javier Aguirre y con el propio jugador para comprobar cuales son los planes del técnico y del jugador en los próximos encuentros. La mañana en la Ciudad Deportiva estuvo cargada. Se conoció, tras la información adelantada por Radio Valencia que Braulio ha fichado, a través de Domingo Catoira, que llegará más adelante, a un miembro contrastado para la dirección deportiva. Se trata de Pachu Martínez, ex del Valladolid que ya trabajó con Catoira en el pasado.

articles.title: Man Utd: Breaking down their tactics after Bruno Fernandes criticism
articles.summary: Was Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes correct in his analysis of his side's tactics in their 4-1 thrashing by Italian side Como?
articles.body:
Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes appeared to question their tactical approach after Wednesday's 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como.

"We started off on the wrong foot," the Portuguese said. "They scored very early, [we had] not much pressure on the ball.

"It's a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave some space behind, to try and get the ball in the first moment [by] waiting for them, [giving] them the ball.

"Sometimes when you give too much of the ball to these teams, they get confidence. They have so many bodies behind the ball, they make you run a lot, people get frustrated."

His quotes are tactically dense so warrant breaking down, but what did Fernandes mean, and does he have a point?

Since Michael Carrick became United manager in January, they have largely defended in a zonal 4-2-4 or 4-4-2 shape that springs into a press in moments.

When Fernandes said United "leave some space behind, to try and get the ball in the first moment" he was referring to them not immediately pressing across the pitch in a man-to-man fashion.

Holding their 4-2-4 shape a little bit deeper, United allow opposition defenders time and space on the ball, looking to set traps before pouncing.

The overarching idea is with four players narrow and high, United's attackers are well positioned to score from turnovers should they win the ball back.

At times during Carrick's stint as caretaker head coach last season, it worked well - as we saw when Bryan Mbeumo scored in United's 3-2 win at Arsenal in January two weeks after Carrick took over

But the same approach has been less effective this season.

On the same night defender Lisandro Martinez questioned United's recruitment - after their 2-0 defeat by Atletico Madrid - he also spoke about the ever-changing tactical landscape.

"You can't stay with what you did last season." he said. "Teams know you, how you play, know every detail, and if you don't change, next season is a big problem."

Last season, the introduction of the 4-2-4 shape as a defensive tactic caught a number of teams off guard, making it more effective.

Pep Guardiola and Pep Lijnders used the same shape at Manchester City - a tweak that underpinned their Carabao Cup final win over an ill-prepared Arsenal .

Having replaced Guardiola, Enzo Maresca redeployed it for the Community Shield in August, but this time Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta had the solutions and the Gunners won.

Within a few games, Maresca had abandoned the 4-24 and moved to a more man-to-man style of defending.

Perhaps that is the sort of change Fernandes is hoping for - recognising the reduced effectiveness of United's defensive approach, with signs of weakness visible as early as pre-season.

AC Milan - now managed by former United boss Ruben Amorim - repeatedly found joy playing around the 4-2-4, with a back five that outnumbered the Red Devils' front four.

United's two central attackers would look to block passes into Milan's midfield two before pressing the central defenders.

The wide position of one of the central defenders would force a United winger to step out, and Milan's wing-back - dropping deep and wide - gave them an easy way out.

United's full-back would then have to cover a large distance to close down the wing-back but by the time pressure was applied, the ball was gone.

The same problems were seen in United's defeat by Atletico Madrid.

Atletico took the risk of employing the same tactic with a back four rather than a back five, which left them an extra attacker high up the pitch.

As United's front two looked to stop passes into the central midfielders, the wide position of the centre-backs drew out United's wingers.

That, in turn, meant left-back Alejandro Grimaldo found himself in space out wide.

This required Diogo Dalot, or if he was pinned back by winger Alex Baena, Youri Tielemans to cover large distances in an attempt to apply some pressure to Grimaldo.

So while Fernandes may have been referring to himself when he said "they make you run a lot, people get frustrated", it could easily have applied to these team-mates.

When Fernandes' quotes were put to Carrick after the game, he pushed back.

"We actually half-pressed, man-to-man in the second half and then ended up conceding a goal from that," he said.

"It's a little bit on whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, but if you don't run and you don't run forward and you don't run back, you aren't going to win."

While the less aggressive 4-2-4 has its weaknesses, it often leaves an extra player in the backline, giving United a numerical advantage in defence.

It also aims to funnel attacks down the flanks, where they are - in theory - less dangerous than chances conceded through the middle.

United's backline have also - under both Carrick and Amorim - struggled to track and duel with their opponents in one-against-one situations when they have committed to a full press.

When using a man-to-man press, losing an individual battle, or lacking the intensity to arrive at your opposing player quickly, makes the system fall apart as we saw for Como's second goal.

In the Premier League, United have also had spells during which they have attempted to press in a more man-to-man fashion, but these have also been imperfectly executed.

In fact, against Spurs , it was Fernandes who misread moments and positioned himself incorrectly.

Despite Amorim's flaws, one of his strengths was in improving United's physical base and intensity. There is a question as to whether Carrick's United, with one game a week last season, were beneficiaries of that.

This season they look unable to sustain the intensity to execute a man-to-man press with the effectiveness of, say, Fabian Hurzeler's Brighton - a physically fit squad aligned on how and when to press.

For United, more concerningly, there appears to be a disconnect - at least in how Fernandes sees the game and the messaging from the coaching staff.

This misalignment makes it hard to execute any defensive approach, with good defending built on intensity and co-ordination between players.

"Sometimes you have to be more brave under pressure," said Fernandes. "Take the risk of pressing high and making them uncomfortable."

But bravery is subjective and one might argue that Carrick defending with four forwards - ready to attack quickly - is an incredibly brave, if not naive, decision.

Going for a 'half man-to-man' approach - looking to lock opponents into one area of the pitch - while allowing some players to defend more zonally feels like a fair trade-off from Carrick.

But how United defend in the 4-2-4 feels outdated already, and is being exposed.

So while both Fernandes and Carrick seem to have a point, if United are to win regularly, any solution this season is likely to lie somewhere in between their views.

articles.title: El mega Mundial sub 15: 3.000 jugadores, 189 selecciones...
articles.standfirst: El torneo de la FIFA más grande de la historia arranca este sábado en Bakú con la presencia de Infantino
articles.summary: El torneo de la FIFA más grande de la historia arranca este sábado en Bakú con la presencia de Infantino
articles.body: El Mundial y Festival sub 15 de la FIFA será un récord en participación ya que estarán representadas nada menos que 189 federaciones miembro. Arranca este sábado con la ceremonia de inauguración y el primer partido y el evento concluirá con la final el 30 de octubre. El Complejo Deportivo Hovsan, construido expresamente para la ocasión en Bakú, la capital de Azerbaiyán, acogerá la mayoría de los partidos de la Copa Mundial y Festival Sub-15 de la FIFA 2026, mientras que las finales de cada categoría se celebrarán en el Crystal Hall de la ciudad. Azerbaiyán fue designado país anfitrión en junio de 2026 . La competición contará con un innovador formato de 8 contra 8, con dos tiempos de 20 minutos cada uno, y en un campo de 68 metros de largo y 47 de ancho. Se disputarán cerca de 1.000 partidos, casi 3.000 jugadores, nacidos en 2011 y 2012, y la infraestructura del torneo permitirá que se jueguen 20 encuentros simultáneos en varios campos, cada uno de los cuales acogerá hasta 10 partidos al día. La idea con esta mega Mundial es ofrecer oportunidades competitivas significativas a aquellas naciones para las que clasificarse para las competiciones de la FIFA sigue siendo un reto enorme. Todos los partidos estarán disponibles en el streaming de FIFA. "Lo más importante es que todos van a jugar hasta el último día, aunque no pases la primera fase", comenta Giovanni Marti, de la FIFA, en una briefing organizado con medios internacionales. Dependiendo de los puntos en sus grupos, las selecciones pasarán a dividirse en 6 niveles de rendimiento para seguir compitiendo hasta el final. "El objetivo es dar oportunidades a todos los jugadores de todo el mundo, la oportunidad de conocerse, de intercambiar experiencias. Es un proyecto muy ambicioso y una experiencia del fútbol juvenil", añade Roberto Grassi, otro miembro de la organización. En 2027 se celebrará el mismo torneo para el fútbol femenino para la misma categoría y en 2028 la idea es que se haga junto ya cada año tanto el masculino o femenino. "La idea de 8 contra 8 es por una decisión tomada por el equipo de Arsène Wenger porque creen que dará más velocidad al juego y porque a los equipos menos estructurados técnicamente les ayuda, porque es en un campo además más pequeño. Permite a todos jugar a todos los niveles, táctico, técnico y físico", apunta Grassi. Sobre la cantidad que ha tenido que invertir la FIFA para este mega torneo, Grassi afirma que hay una colaboración muy estrecha con el Gobierno del país que es quien ha invertido en el complejo y que al final de la competición se ofrecerá un informe detallado al respecto.. La selección española ya está concentrada en Bakú. Hernán Pérez ya ofreció hace diez días la lista de convocados y el seleccionador será David Gordo. España se medirá a Chile el 24 de octubre, a Congo y Tayikistán el 25 de octubre, y a Barbados y Kuwait el 26 de este mismo mes. La lista la forman Danel Castro (Betis), Leo Rico (Villarreal) como porteros. Defensas: Adrián Bielsa (Real Madrid), Iván Castellanos (Atlético de Madrid), Yulian Mosquera (Valencia), Lucas Bernal (Barcelona). Centrocampistas: Bruno Fernández (Betis), Víctor Barbany (Barcelona), Alberto Ruíz (Real Madrid), Tiago Polo (Betis), Ricardo Pérez (Valencia). Delanteros: Hugo Oliva (Espanyol), Mikel López (Real Madrid) y Divine Ikenna (Barcelona)

articles.title: Va de récord: Carrión será el quinto técnico del Lega en poco más de un año
articles.standfirst: El club pepinero busca la estabilidad no encontrada hasta ahora con un entrenador al que llevaba tiempo siguiendo
articles.summary: El club pepinero busca la estabilidad no encontrada hasta ahora con un entrenador al que llevaba tiempo siguiendo
articles.body: Luis Carrión será el quinto entrenador que se siente en el banquillo del Leganés, dirigirá al equipo pepinero por primera vez el sábado ante el Mallorca, desde el descenso a Segunda división en mayo de 2025. Una cifra que refleja la inestabilidad que ha vivido el conjunto pepinero en los últimos meses, sin encontrar todavía la continuidad necesaria para consolidar un proyecto deportivo. Todo comenzó con la salida de Borja Jiménez tras perder la categoría. Paco López fue el elegido para iniciar una nueva etapa, pero su aventura terminó en diciembre. Su sustituto, Igor Oca, tampoco consiguió cambiar la dinámica y acabó dejando su puesto a Carlos Martínez, que asumió el equipo para una auténtica final por la permanencia ante el Mirandés. Superado aquel momento, el Leganés apostó por Rubén Albés para liderar un proyecto ambicioso, con Álvaro Morata como uno de sus grandes referentes. Sin embargo, los resultados volvieron a precipitar los acontecimientos. Cuatro derrotas consecutivas, sin marcar un solo gol, terminaron por agotar el crédito del técnico gallego. Pese a tantos movimientos, el objetivo del club sigue siendo el mismo: encontrar un entrenador que aporte estabilidad y pueda desarrollar un proyecto a largo plazo. Y en ese escenario aparece Luis Carrión, un técnico que llevaba tiempo en los planes de la entidad. De hecho, el propio Carrión reconoció en rueda de prensa que ya había mantenido negociaciones con el Leganés en temporadas anteriores, aunque su llegada nunca terminó de concretarse. Ahora ambas partes han encontrado el momento para unir sus caminos. El club confía en su experiencia y en una propuesta futbolística diferente para recuperar la competitividad y la ilusión en Butarque. Carrión tendrá por delante el reto de levantar a un equipo necesitado de resultados, pero también de convertirse en ese entrenador capaz de dar continuidad a un proyecto que, desde el descenso, todavía busca su sitio. El Ontime Butarque ante el Real Mallorca será la primera parada en el viaje de Carrión en el Leganés.

articles.title: Man Utd boss Michael Carrick and captain Bruno Fernandes clash over tactics in Como defeat - but who was right?
articles.summary: Man Utd have not won for seven matches and captain Bruno Fernandes openly questioned the tactics of his head coach Michael Carrick after a crushing 4-1 defeat to Como in the Champions League - here we dig into the numbers to find out who was right
articles.body:
Fernandes said United gave Como too much time and space in possession and blamed this on the staff's decision not to press man to man.

United have been attempting to press man to man at times this season, often with bad outcomes. You can see just how ill-suited the current group are for that approach here.

Fernandes is not wrong to say United gave Como a lot of space. The Italian side completed 600 passes, which is more than any other team in a game against United this season.

In fact, the three games when opposition teams have completed most passes against United have come in the last three games against Como, Atletico Madrid and Leeds. This has coincided with Carrick's attempts to be more compact and solid defensively.

United, on a seven-match winless run, have not won any of those games. However, at Leeds (1-1 draw) and Atletico Madrid (2-0 defeat) there were signs of improvement in terms of defensive shape.

There was no such defensive solidity or compactness in Italy. But Como's chances did not come after long passing sequences. The most passes leading to a Como shot was 13, culminating in their fourth goal.

For context, this season the longest opposition passing sequence leading to a shot against United was 45 passes against Fulham in September. The reality is that Como chose their moments and efficiently cut through United with ease.

The United captain's claim that Como had showed United how it should have been done with regard to the press is also undermined by the numbers: Como won the ball back in the attacking third five times compared to United's four.

Fernandes also claimed that United were tired as a result of sitting off Como and chasing the ball down for most of the game which led to mistakes.

However, the fact Como's first two goals, the most crucial in terms of momentum, came within five minutes of the whistle going for kick-off and the second half suggest that Fernandes' conclusion is flawed.

For the opener, which came inside two minutes, United's backline were sat deep to defend their box, and the midfielders were ambling back in support.

United had seven players to the hosts' five in the defensive third, which in theory should have been enough to keep Como out.

However, Matheus Cunha allowed Nico Paz to drift into a big pocket of space on the edge of the box. Harry Maguire then backed off the Argentina international before he scored.

Paz was surrounded by four United players when he curled the ball into the far corner.

It does not help Fernandes' argument that it was Carlos Baleba that made the error in posession for Como's third goal less than 15 minutes after being brought on. He can hardly claim to have been knackered already.

Was man-to-man pressing the problem for Como's second?

Carrick said United "half pressed man to man" in the second half and conceded as a result as he jabbed back at Fernandes when asked about his captain's comment in a post-match press conference. And he does have a point.

United's shape out of possession for Como's second goal - which came four minutes into the second half - was more of a mid-block. The press was triggered as Como entered the middle third of the pitch.

Baleba pressured Lucas Da Cunha as he received the ball and Noussair Mazraoui stepped inside to pressure Martin Baturina when the ball was shifted inside to him. Neither of them got anywhere near their man.

The big gap between the centre-backs and the midfield was then exposed by two simple Como passes.

The rest of the United players jogged back with little intensity as they watched Como progress the ball into the final third to create a 3v3 scenario from which Anastasios Douvikas scored.

Carrick has persisted with Maguire and Lisandro Martinez at centre-back this season when pressing man-to-man despite neither being suitable. Nor is Matthijs de Ligt, who started against Como after a long injury lay-off, as shown by the tumble he took before Como's second goal.

Having at least one defender with the agility and speed to make recovery runs, is a non-negotiable for any team hoping to employ man-to-man pressing. Leny Yoro is more suitable yet continues to start at right-back or on the bench.

If Carrick does want this team to get to a point where they can press man-to-man, he needs to select players more suited to that style of football. At the moment his options are limited but he is not helping himself.

Was it down to a lack of effort from Man Utd?

Carrick's other point was that whatever tactics United use, it will not matter if they fail to run back. The lack of effort was clear - as it has been often this season - throughout the match on Tuesday.

For Como's second and fourth goals, in particular, United's failure to track back was alarming.

Fernandes, Youri Tielemans and Bryan Mbeumo, United's front three, were walking back as Como scored their second and stood all the way back at the halfway line. Beyond Baleba and Mazraoui, as mentioned above, there was little intensity from anyone else defensively.

Como's fourth goal was most damning. Maguire was out of position and trying to make up the ground, which left the eventual goalscorer Jacobo Ramon with a big space to run. One of Baleba or Diogo Dalot, both of whom are much quicker, had to bust a gut to cover.

There was no awareness of the danger from either. Dalot was not in picture by the time Ramon headed in. Baleba, signed to add legs to United's midfield, was overtaken by the 33-year-old Maguire, who turned straight to the £70m signing after the ball went in to lambast him.

It sums up United's issues that a new signing, whose arrival had brought so much hope, has already got into the bad habits of his team-mates after just a handful of appearances.

articles.title: Real Madrid’s complaint over La Liga chief’s Nazi slant sent to tribunal
articles.summary: La Liga ⁠chief ⁠Javier Tebas compared Real Madrid’s communication to Nazi propaganda and now faces a tribunal in Spain.
articles.body:
La Liga President Javier Tebas could face disciplinary action for comparing Real Madrid’s communication methods with those of Nazi propaganda minister Joseph Goebbels, after Spain’s National Sports Council (CSD) asked the country’s sports tribunal on Thursday to assess whether the football executive had committed an offence.

The CSD said in a statement that it had referred the matter to the country’s Administrative Court for Sport (TAD) after Tebas made the comparison in a post on social media platform X on October 16.

The TAD must determine whether Tebas’s comments could constitute a serious offence under Spain’s 1990 Sports Law, which includes “notorious and public acts that harm sporting dignity or decorum”.

The CSD said, “It is essential to preserve the values that make sport a space of respect, coexistence, and fair play.”

Spanish giants Real Madrid called for Tebas, 64, to resign after he criticised their efforts to discredit refereeing in Spain.

Tebas had said Real Madrid’s in-house TV channel often suggested that referees attempt to prevent the club from winning.

The outspoken Spanish league chief said these tactics “recall propaganda mechanisms exploited by Goebbels”.

Tebas later attempted to clarify that he was drawing comparisons with “those propaganda techniques” and not with the ideology of the Nazis.

The La Liga chief reiterated on Thursday with another X post that his comment had “distinguished between propaganda techniques and ideology”.

Tebas also questioned why Madrid, in “accusing the refereeing system of corruption”, did “not affect sporting dignity and decorum”.

“Does it not harm clubs, referees, and millions of fans?” wrote Tebas. “Or do those values only deserve a public defence when someone responds to such attacks?”

Real Madrid criticise referees most weeks on their television channel, and last year accused officiating in Spain of being “rigged” and “totally discredited”.

La Liga ‌did ‌not immediately respond to a request for comment.

articles.body: Alexia Putellas colecciona premios y reconocimientos por doquier. Uno que no tiene en la larga lista de galardones recibidos hasta la fecha es el de Los 100 de MARCA, distinción que ha logrado tras recibir 458 puntos en las votaciones, superando a Patri Guijarro (422) y Ewa Pajor (298), ambas compañeras en el Barcelona la temporada pasada. La de Mollet del Vallés fue la futbolista más valorada por los 40 periodistas especializados en el mal llamado fútbol femenino, contando con especialistas del Universo MARCA, así como de compañer@s a nivel nacional e internacional. Alexia compartió el podio con Patri Guijarro, a la que aventajó en 36 puntos; y con Ewa Pajor, a la que sacó 160 puntos de ventaja. El resto de españolas en la lista de nominadas fueron Claudia Pina, séptima; Mariona Caldentey, duodécima; Cata Coll, decimocuarta; Mapi León, vigésimotercera. El envés de la moneda lo protagonizaron Melvine Malard, Momoko Tanikawa y Tessa Wullaert, que no recibieron un solo voto. Alexia, que se despidió del Barcelona a final de temporada tras 14 cursos de azulgrana, fue gran protagonista del éxito culé. articles.title: Bruno Fernandes to remain Man Utd captain despite outburst
articles.summary: Bruno Fernandes will remain as Manchester United captain and will not be disciplined for his post-match criticism of Michael Carrick after the 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como.
articles.body:
Bruno Fernandes will remain as Manchester United captain and will not be disciplined for his post-match criticism of Michael Carrick after the 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como .

The United skipper criticised Carrick's tactics for the game, then said it was up to the United head coach and his backroom team, not the players, to spot any issues and change them.

It was seen by many externally as a challenge to Carrick's authority, just eight days after United defender Lisandro Martinez criticised director of football Jason Wilcox and the club's summer recruitment.

Inside Old Trafford, there is sympathy for Fernandes for the position he found himself in.

The Portugal midfielder did 10 post-match interviews in Como, despite being replaced by Joshua Zirkzee midway through the second half.

While there is disappointment at some of his comments, it is acknowledged Fernandes' annoyance was understandable given the manner of the loss, which was one of the worst in United's European history.

It remains to be seen whether Fernandes will be picked for Sunday's Premier League encounter with Bournemouth at Old Trafford. Carrick will be asked about the situation when he holds his pre-game news conference at 13:30 BST on Friday.

Carrick carrying on but senior Man Utd figures concerned by performances

Former Manchester United striker Wayne Rooney said he was in "shock" and "disbelief" at the performance against Como and he is as "worried as I've been for a long time" at the situation at Old Trafford.

And, while he understands the questioning of Carrick, a close personal friend of the former England and United skipper, Rooney also called the players "selfish" and said "they're like babies" in the wake of the controversial comments from both Martinez and Fernandes.

"When Martinez came out, I said this is an absolute nightmare because it will rip the dressing room apart," Rooney told the United Stand podcast. "That was the start. We've seen it now with Bruno and you're going to see it with more players because they don't want to take responsibility.

"You can say whether Bruno was right or wrong in what he said but you have to take responsibility on the pitch. You have to take responsibility as a group of players.

"These players, they're selfish. They don't care about their team-mates, don't care about the manager, the staff or the fans, they care about themselves. If they're not getting what's right for them, they're like babies and just throw their toys out of the pram and go and deflect the blame on to anyone else but themselves."

Fernandes' form has dipped markedly from last season, when he was named PFA and FWA Player of the Year and broke the Premier League record for assists in a single season.

"He [Fernandes] is putting pressure on someone else because he doesn't want to face it," added Rooney.

"If he looks at himself in the mirror, if Martinez and all of them looked at themselves in the mirror, they'll find what's looking back at them is them, and that's not good enough. They need to show more."

Rooney has also called on the Manchester United board to provide clarity on the future of Carrick, who he believes needs to "come out fighting".

Carrick will be in charge for Sunday's visit of Bournemouth despite intense speculation he is on the brink of dismissal following United's worst run of form since 2015-16.

"I was in that situation [at Plymouth and Birmingham City] and I can only say now, looking back and reflecting, if I was in Michael Carrick's position now, I'd come out fighting," said Rooney.

"There's no more Mr Nice Guy. There are certain things you've got to do to protect them players, but you have to come out fighting for yourself because those players will drag you down and it's going to be you who's going to lose your job over it."

articles.title: Armando Sadiku cuelga las botas
articles.standfirst: El delantero albanés jugó en el Levante, Málaga, Las Palmas y Cartagena
articles.summary: El delantero albanés jugó en el Levante, Málaga, Las Palmas y Cartagena
articles.body: Armando Sadiku pone punto final a su carrera como futbolista profesional a los 35 años. El delantero albanés ha anunciado su retirada después de casi dos décadas compitiendo en distintos países y continentes. Su siguiente destino seguirá ligado al fútbol, aunque desde otra posición: asumirá la dirección deportiva del Bellinzona suizo, el último club de su trayectoria. "Gracias, fútbol. Te echaré de menos". Con estas palabras se ha despedido el atacante, que deja atrás una carrera marcada por los cambios de equipo, las experiencias internacionales y algunos momentos que quedarán en el recuerdo de los aficionados de su país. Sadiku dio sus primeros pasos en el fútbol albanés, pero encontró en Suiza un escenario importante para crecer como delantero. Sus etapas en el Locarno y el Lugano le ayudaron a abrirse camino, antes de pasar por el Zúrich, el Vaduz y el Legia de Varsovia. En enero de 2018 aterrizó en España para incorporarse al Levante, aunque su participación en Primera División fue limitada. Un año y medio después, el Málaga le ofreció una nueva oportunidad en Segunda. El verano de 2019 llevó a Sadiku a La Rosaleda en calidad de cedido. El delantero llegó en un momento especialmente delicado para el club, que atravesaba una profunda crisis económica y tuvo que construir una plantilla condicionada por las dificultades financieras. En medio de aquel escenario, el albanés respondió con goles. Durante la temporada 2019/20 disputó 36 encuentros ligueros y anotó 13 tantos, convirtiéndose en el máximo goleador del Málaga. Su aportación resultó importante para un equipo que tuvo que afrontar el curso con numerosos obstáculos y que encontró en el atacante una referencia en el área rival. Sin embargo, su etapa como blanquiazul duró únicamente una temporada. Una vez finalizada la cesión, Sadiku continuó su carrera lejos de Martiricos, dejando atrás uno de los capítulos más destacados de su paso por el fútbol español. Después jugó en el Erzurumspor turco y en el Bolívar boliviano. Más adelante regresó a España para defender los colores de Las Palmas y el Cartagena. Su recorrido internacional también incluyó una experiencia en la India, donde militó en el Mohun Bagan y el FC Goa, antes de regresar a Suiza para cerrar su carrera en el Bellinzona. Si hay un momento que define la trayectoria de Sadiku, ese se encuentra en la Eurocopa de 2016. El delantero fue el autor del gol con el que Albania derrotó a Rumanía por 1-0 en la fase de grupos del torneo disputado en Francia. Aquel triunfo fue el primero de la selección albanesa en una fase final de una Eurocopa y convirtió al atacante en una figura recordada por los seguidores de su país. Su trayectoria internacional concluyó con 12 goles en 38 partidos con Albania. Un balance que refuerza su lugar entre los delanteros destacados de la historia reciente de la selección. Ahora, Sadiku inicia una etapa diferente. El futbolista que pasó por ligas de Europa, Sudamérica y Asia cambia las botas por los despachos y asumirá la dirección deportiva del Bellinzona. Su carrera deja goles, numerosos destinos y, sobre todo, una noche inolvidable para el fútbol albanés. En Málaga también quedará el recuerdo de aquel delantero que firmó 13 tantos en una temporada marcada por las dificultades.

articles.title: Premier League predictions: Chris Sutton v Waffle the Wonder Dog and his owner, Simon - & AI
articles.summary: BBC Sport football expert Chris Sutton takes on Waffle the Wonder Dog and his owner Simon, plus the BBC readers and AI with his predictions for this weekend's Premier League fixtures.
articles.body:
Manchester City have won their first seven Premier League games of the season but will their 100% record survive Saturday's trip to an improving Aston Villa side?

"Villa have beaten City in this fixture in each of the past three years under Unai Emery," said BBC Sport football expert Chris Sutton.

"They will fancy it this time too - they are seven unbeaten in all competitions, and flying at the moment."

Sutton is making predictions for all 380 Premier League games this season, against AI, BBC Sport readers and a variety of guests.

For week eight, he takes on Waffle the Wonder Dog and his owner Simon, who is played by actor James Merry.

Waffle's After School Club, featuring James and Waffle, is available on CBeebies and BBC iPlayer right now, with lots of fun after-school adventures for families to enjoy together.

Do you agree with their predictions? You can pick your own below.

The most popular scoreline selected for each game is used in the scoreboards and tables at the bottom of this page.

A correct result (picking a win, draw or defeat) is worth 10 points. The exact score earns 40 points.

Want to make more predictions? You can play BBC Sport's new Match of the Day predictor game every week, featuring six fixtures from domestic and European competition.

Waffle is a talking dog whose adventures on his show often end in chaos for Simon and the rest of his family.

Like most dogs, he loves football - or at least loves chasing one.

"I am an enthusiastic baller," Waffle told BBC Sport. "But technically my best position is right-back... on the sofa.

"My favourite player is the England captain, Harry Kane-9, and I'm a Liverpool fan so my all-time hero is Kenny Dog-leash.

"My fur is red and I am a poodle so of course I support the Reds, or Liverpoodle as I like to call them - they never walkies alone."

In real life, actor James Merry is an Aston Villa fan, who has a long connection with the club.

"I grew up in Sutton Coldfield, north Birmingham, and just about everyone is Villa there," he told BBC Sport.

"My mum's side of the family are all fans - my great-aunt was a season-ticket holder for about 40 years and my nan lived most of her life on Witton Road, which is just round the corner from Villa Park.

"My first job was there too - when I was 16 I worked in the catering department serving burgers on matchdays.

"Then, during the summer I had to clean every executive box and polish all the cutlery and make sure everywhere was properly stocked.

"We had the run of Villa Park and I was like a kid in a candy shop."

Chris Sutton, Waffle the Wonder Dog and James Merry were speaking to BBC Sport's Chris Bevan.

The AI predictions were generated using Microsoft Copilot Chat - we simply asked the tool to 'predict this weekend's Premier League scores'.

So, I am up against a talking dog this week? I'm not sure that improves my chances of winning - I've been barking up the wrong tree with my predictions all season anyway.

One of us has got to beat AI though - I've been reading about it in the news and it is not just with football scores where it seems to be taking over.

This game is a tough one to call, though. It is going to be very tight.

Nottingham Forest can't score. That's their issue, and they have only managed five goals in their first seven league games.

It did make me laugh when I read that Forest boss Oliver Glasner had got Chris Wood to give advice to the other strikers about finishing - why not just play Wood then?

Ipswich are still bottom of the league table based on my predictions (see bottom of page) but they ran Manchester City close in the end last week and are doing better than everyone expected, myself included.

I like what Tractor Boys boss Gary O'Neil is doing there, and they already have three league wins from seven games - the last time they were in the Premier League, in 2024-25, they only managed four all season.

Forest are second bottom and could really do with getting something here, and Ipswich haven't drawn a game yet - so that's what I am going for.

James' prediction: The director of Waffle, Tim Hopewell, is a Forest fan and I have gone for them here. I like the way they play. 1-2

Villa have hit a bit of form and seem to be getting back to the level they were at last season.

They had another good win in the Champions League this week, but then you'd expect them to beat Viking pretty comfortably.

Emery's side played well against Newcastle last week too but I thought Newcastle were a bit too gung-ho, and paid the price. City are a lot more streetwise.

City are going to slip up eventually this season but the fact they have lost on their past three visits to Villa Park actually makes me think it will be different this time.

Erling Haaland is fit too, which will obviously help. With all the heat on the club at the moment it could just turn out to be one of those seasons where they continue on this incredible run.

Waffle the Wonder Dog's prediction: Ross BARKley gets two for Villa, but Erling HOWLand to score a hat-trick. Sorry, dad! 2-3

James' favourite Villa players: The early to mid-'90s was the time when I was getting into football so Dean Saunders and Dalian Atkinson were my heroes, and Paul McGrath as well. That was certainly a golden era - I need to mention Shaun Teale too, because he was always a favourite. I think I had his name on the back of a shirt.

Now? I think most people of my generation would pick John McGinn. He is an absolute club legend for what he has done for us down the years and my shirt now has got McGinn on the back.

James on Villa's season: We seem to be picking up some form after another slow start. It looks like Johan Manzambi is going to be pivotal for us this season and Nicolas Jackson has started well, he has stuck a few away.

This might sound a bit bonkers but, with Emery's record in Europe, I am more excited about that than what we might do domestically, because I think we might go deep in the Champions League.

James' prediction: Because we are weak at the back at the moment I think City will score two or three, but we are looking lively up front and could do the same. I've got to be partisan - and I am also going to go for a barnstormer. 3-2

Arsenal were so ugly in the way they beat Nottingham Forest last weekend, but were a lot easier on the eye in the midweek draw with Bayern Munich.

They are going to be without the injured Bukayo Saka for this game, but they are at home and they should still have too much for Everton .

Everton will make it tough for them, of course, but I am not sure how they will hurt the Gunners.

James' prediction: Arsenal are just a machine at home. 3-1

Whoever loses this is likely to end the day in the relegation zone.

Sometimes these kind of games can be quite cagey, with both teams afraid of being beaten, but here I feel like Coventry and Fulham will have a go and there could be a few goals flying in.

Coventry have a bit about them going forward, especially when they use their pace on the counter-attack, but they are also a bit vulnerable defensively.

Because of that, I am going to go with Fulham . They got their first win of the season against Hull last week and they are definitely capable of getting another one here.

James' prediction: My old man is a Coventry fan - he was born and bred in Cov but then married a Brummie and moved to Birmingham so he was always on a hiding to nothing trying to get me to support Coventry . He won't be happy because I've gone for a draw here. 1-1

We were talking on the Monday Night Club about what Chelsea could do this season without any European football.

Tottenham are not in Europe either, of course, but they don't look like they are going to be challenging at the top of the table the way Xabi Alonso's side are.

People keep saying how Chelsea 's attack is so good, but their 2-0 win over Everton last time out was their first clean sheet of their campaign in the league, and that side of thing still needs to improve.

Spurs , meanwhile, do seem to be getting better, albeit slowly.

It was a big result for them to beat Coventry on Monday but they have an awful record at Stamford Bridge, with only one win there in the Premier League era.

I don't see them getting anything this time, either.

Waffle the Wonder Dog's prediction: Archie GrayHOUND will score a couple for Spurs , but I'm backing Chelsea because I was a fan of Didier DOGba back in the day. 4-2

James' prediction: Chelsea carry so much attacking threat. 3-1

Crystal Palace manager Pierre Sage's future appears to be in some doubt but his critics seem to have forgotten that they are 14th in the table, when the Eagles finished 15th last season under Oliver Glasner.

Yes, Palace had a heavy defeat at Brighton last week and it doesn't help it was at the hands of their big rivals, but it is not like Sage has got one point from his first seven games. They are leaking a few goals, but there are reasons for that.

There has been huge change at Selhurst Park in recent months, with some key players leaving, especially at the back. Others have stayed but are still unhappy, and Sage has had a lot to contend with.

Palace play in Turkey on Thursday night which won't help their preparation for this game, but I still feel like they will get something against Newcastle .

There has been a lot of change at the Magpies too, but the thing that worries me most about Matthias Jaissle's side is that they are so open.

'Chaotic' was the word I used to describe them against Aston Villa last week.

Villa are always very well structured in the way they play but they got chances against Newcastle just by persevering with their build-up play.

If Newcastle don't get their press quite right again here, then Palace will cause them problems too - I definitely don't see this game as being one where defences are on top.

James' prediction: Both teams will be happy just to get a point on the board. 1-1

Although Hull have made a great start I still think they will get relegated.

We know they will have a go at Brentford , but the Bees will be too smart for them.

Brentford would have beaten Liverpool last week without Yehor Yarmoliuk's stupid red card. If they can keep 11 men on the pitch, they will win this one.

James' prediction: Brentford are such an amazingly well-run club with what they have achieved. They are going to be too strong for Hull . 1-2

Liverpool have an extra 48 hours to prepare for this game - they played Villarreal at home on Tuesday, while Brighton are away in the Czech Republic on Thursday.

I don't think it will make any difference, though, because the way that the Seagulls play, I am expecting them to go to Anfield and win.

This has the makings of a great game but, while Liverpool have had a couple of good results, I am still not convinced by them.

Andoni Iraola's side are a work in progress with a tendency to empty their midfield and that means Brighton can hurt them.

Waffle the Wonder Dog's prediction: A win for the Liverpoodles! 2-1

James' prediction: This is going to be close. Brighton are playing really well but I am still going to back Liverpool at Anfield. 2-1

After all the stick I got from Manchester United fans for saying they would get thumped by Leeds last weekend, it turns out I was only a few days out - it happened against Como instead.

United have been poor all season, though. That's why I went for them to be despatched like that - the 5-0 scoreline was a little bit tongue in cheek, but the point I was making has been proven this week.

The Bruno Fernandes criticism of Michael Carrick just adds to the problems United have at the moment - it is as if they are at the stage now where you have to pick who you want to back.

I don't know where United go from here but I am going for a Bournemouth win - the Cherries will attack them, and their great recent record at Old Trafford will give them confidence too.

If United do lose, I think it will be the end for Carrick because I just don't see how he survives this.

Even if United get something from this game, it is still just a matter of time before he goes.

Waffle the Wonder Dog's prediction: BARKus Rashford to win this for United. 2-1

James' prediction: Carrick really needs a win and they are at home so I think he will get it. 2-0

Sunderland have killed me this season because I just don't seem to be able to predict them at all.

The Black Cats are bottom of the table after losing four league games in a row and their boss Regis le Bris has a few problems to solve.

One of them is having European football that stretches their squad - they are away in Poland on Thursday - but at least they will have striker Brian Brobbey back from injury at the weekend.

After last weekend's loss at Bournemouth , Sunderland defender Nordi Mukiele suggested the Black Cats may have become "arrogant", but I don't see that outburst being as damaging as the ones by Manchester United players recently.

Still, things like that are better kept inside the dressing room because some of Mukiele's team-mates will be asking him if he was calling them arrogant.

I was never arrogant as a player, by the way, but people used to call me far worse than that in my day.

Maybe we will see a reaction from Sunderland here, but I still don't see them winning this because Leeds are battle-hardened and are a good team too.

They weren't at their best against Manchester United but still picked up a point, and they won't be leaving the Stadium of Light empty-handed.

Waffle the Wonder Dog's prediction: I like the sound of LEADS United and I love playing with George the cat (who lives next door) but 11 Black Cats means it's hide-behind-the-sofa time! 0-2

James' prediction: I had a look at all the fixtures and I thought one of them has got to finish 0-0, hasn't it? I have gone for this one. 0-0

Chris and the BBC readers both got six correct results with no exact scores from the 10 games in week seven, giving them 60 points apiece.

His guest, boxer and Ipswich fan Fabio Wardley, did better with four correct results, including one exact score - Bournemouth 's 2-0 win over Sunderland - for a total of 70 points.

But, for the third week in a row, AI took the weekly win.

It managed eight correct results, including one exact score - Liverpool 's 2-1 victory at Brentford - for a total of 110 points.

Like last week, there was only one game where everyone picked the right outcome - Brighton 's 5-0 victory over Crystal Palace - although again hardly anyone got the correct score.

From almost 30,000 predictions, the most popular scoreline was a 2-0 Seagulls win. Almost 8,000 of you went for that, but well done to the 57 of you who got it spot-on.

articles.title: FIFA announces USA to host first Women’s Club World Cup in 2028
articles.summary: FIFA to stage inaugural Women’s Club World Cup, with 16 of football’s top teams, in United States in 2028.
articles.body:
The United States will host the inaugural women’s football Club World Cup in 2028, FIFA announced Thursday.

“The decision was taken in view of its experience in organising FIFA tournaments, the maturity of its infrastructure and services and the level of stakeholder interest in women’s football in the country,” world football’s governing body said.

The US has a proven track record of staging large sporting events, notably cohosting the men’s World Cup earlier this year.

The first women’s Club World Cup will be staged from January 5-30, 2028.

It will bring together 19 top-tier clubs from all six continental confederations.

The AFC (Asia), CAF (Africa), CONCACAF (North America) and CONMEBOL (South America) will be represented by three clubs apiece at the competition, one team will fly the flag for the OFC (Oceania) and six of Europe’s best sides will represent UEFA.

Seven clubs have already secured their berths at the tournament: Arsenal (England), Club America Femenil (Mexico), Barcelona (Spain), Gotham (United States), Naegohyang (North Korea), Corinthians (Brazil) and Wuhan Jiangda (China).

“These seven clubs, and a dozen more, will come together to show the strength and depth of women’s club football to a global audience,” said FIFA chief women’s football officer Sarai Bareman.

“They will have the opportunity to tell their story, expand their fan base and represent their club on the world stage. They have thoroughly earned this opportunity to be part of history in the United States.”

FIFA said the introduction of the tournament marked “a major milestone for the professionalisation and global expansion of the women’s club game, giving elite club sides a true world stage to compete on every four years”.

Initially slated for 2026, FIFA pushed the inaugural tournament back by two years so it enjoys a clear window following the 2027 women’s World Cup and before the 2028 Summer Olympics in Los Angeles.

The US has a proven track record of hosting large sporting events, notably staging the men’s 2026 World Cup, which was won by Spain earlier this year.

Chelsea are the reigning men’s FIFA Club World Cup holders, after beating Paris St Germain in the 2025 final, which was also staged in the US.

articles.title: Karlan Grant: Charlton forward on returning to the club and facing Norwich on Red, White and Black weekend
articles.summary: Karlan Grant has returned to Charlton after seven years away; this weekend celebrates the club's Red, White and Black campaign and the EFL's Together for Racism fixture; watch Charlton vs Norwich live on Sky Sports Football and Main Event from 11.30am; kick-off 12.30pm
articles.body:
The Addicks academy graduate returned after six years at West Brom, where he had turned down a new deal. "It all aligned at the time and hopefully it's still aligned at the end of the season," he added of why he decided to come back to south London.

When Grant left The Valley in January 2019 for Huddersfield, it was not well-received by some Charlton fans. But seven years and three clubs later, the 29-year-old is an experienced and established Championship player.

"I think experience is a big thing," the forward exclusively told Sky Sports. "I left so young, I've played a lot of games since then, so it's just bringing my experience to the group.

"I got a bit of stick when I did leave, but that's football. Coming back, I'm one of them, so it's been good."

Charlton's academy is famous for producing talented players, and is perhaps demonstrated no better than an Addicks forward line that comprises three graduates - Tyreece Campbell, Miles Leaburn and Grant.

"They're good lads. They've done very well to get to this level. I'm here to help with my experience and help the team as well, so it's nice to see them do what they're doing," he said of his now team-mates.

Alan Mwamba is the latest academy product making waves in the first team - Grant also tipping Ruben Reid as one to watch - with south London well-known as a hotbed for scouting.

It is the location that helps Charlton's academy thrive, with Grant also pointing to the staff as key in helping players develop.

"The coaches here are amazing," he said. "The location in the south east [of London], I was lucky to play with players coming through who have played for England and at the highest level. The pathway has always been there and will always be there.

"That was me when I was a kid, playing cage football. Coming through the community, there's a lot of opportunity here and if kids find their time and believe in the system throughout their youth, they will definitely get a chance.

"I think every year, there will be someone to keep an eye on. There's so many."

On Saturday, Charlton, without a win in their past eight league games, take on Norwich, a side also short of form as they sit just above the bottom three.

It is the club's annual Red, White and Black weekend, which reinforces the club's commitment to equality, diversity and inclusion.

Each year, there is a parade to The Valley including local students and community groups. For the first time, the march will be held ahead of Charlton Women's game against Chelsea Women on Sunday.

The men's match is also dedicated to the EFL's Together Against Racism campaign. Grant, alongside Charlie Kelman, attended a Show Racism the Red Card workshop at The Valley as part of the Charlton Athletic Community Trust's Premier League Primary Stars programme.

"These events are so important because us as players can really help people outside of the football environment," Grant said.

"Football is such a big sport and everyone looks into it and there's a lot of diversity and different cultures within the club.

"It brings everyone together and it just shows that even in football and outside of football, it's so important."

articles.title: Man Utd boss Michael Carrick remaining in charge vs Bournemouth amid growing concerns at Old Trafford
articles.summary: Watch Man Utd vs Bournemouth in the Premier League on Sunday from 12.30pm on Sky Sports Main Event; kick-off 2pm; Man Utd without a win in seven matches; Bruno Fernandes likely to avoid punishment for criticism of coach's tactics after thrashing in Como
articles.body:
There is a feeling both inside and outside Old Trafford that Sunday's Premier League match - live on Sky Sports - could be pivotal in determining Carrick's future.

No decision has been taken about plans beyond Sunday as things stand following Wednesday's 4-1 defeat to Como in the Champions League.

Bruno Fernandes will not be stripped of the captaincy in light of his criticism of the United coaching staff and is unlikely to face any punishment for his comments after the crushing defeat in Italy.

There is a feeling within the Carrington training ground that the performance and result in the Champions League on Wednesday night was unacceptable - as Carrick himself said after the match.

There is sympathy for Carrick when it comes to the injury problems he is dealing with, and many United supporters agreed with Lisandro Martinez's outspoken views of last week when he said the squad is not strong enough to compete at the top level. Martinez levelled the criticism at the United hierarchy, not the head coach.

But it is clear United's bosses feel that, despite those factors, the squad is stronger than it was last season when Carrick secured a third-placed Premier League finish, and so far this season the team has woefully underperformed.

United's directors assessed and interviewed a host of other candidates in January as part of their due diligence before appointing Carrick, and while it is thought there has been no formal contact with those candidates recently, such discussions cannot be ruled out in the coming days.

Fernandes unlikely to be punished for criticism of staff

Fernandes will not be stripped of the Manchester United captaincy and is unlikely to be disciplined by the club following his criticism of the coaching staff and the tactics in the 4-1 defeat to Como.

Sky Sports News has been told that, while there is disappointment within the club with what last season's PFA Player of the Year said post-match, the wider feeling is that he was voicing an understandable frustration and anger at the manner of the defeat.

A string of ex-professionals have lined up to criticise Fernandes, with Jamie Carragher calling him "an absolute disgrace".

In his own post-match news conference, head coach Carrick responded to his captain's comments by saying: "If you don't run back, you ain't going to win."

Asked by TNT Sports about a lack of cohesion in United's work out of possession, Fernandes defended his team-mates and put the blame on Carrick and his coaches on Wednesday night.

"It's a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man, and sometimes leave a little space in behind and try to get the ball in the first moment, to wait for them, to give them the ball," he said.

"But sometimes when you give too much the ball to these teams they get confident, they have so many bodies behind the ball that make you run a lot, make people get frustrated, and then obviously when you recover the ball the legs are, and the brain, much more difficult to make it work."

Was that tactical idea what cost Man Utd in Como? "That's on the manager and on the staff to see it, it's not on me," said Fernandes.

"I just said, I think sometimes we have to be more brave on the pressure, trying to take a risk of getting that press very high and making them uncomfortable - as they did to us."

Carra calls Fernandes comments 'a disgrace'

Carragher has criticised Fernandes for questioning Man Utd's tactics following their defeat to Como, but believes that it could be the end of the line for Carrick.

"We said Lisandro Martinez was bang out of order for calling out the hierarchy," Carragher said on CBS Sports .

"For Bruno Fernandes to do that, it is a disgrace. Last season he was Player of the Year. That was due to Michael Carrick coming in as manager. He wouldn't have got that award without Carrick. He put him back in his right position.

"His attitude and the way he goes about things, it is not right at all. He has reacted like that because he was brought off and he has been embarrassed tonight by the manager.

"When he talks about pressing, whether it is man-to-man or zonal, for years, Bruno Fernandes has meant Man Utd can't press.

"He runs all over the place like a kid in the school yard for the supporters. They all think he's working hard, he is not. He is killing the rest of the team by doing it.

"He is not playing in a successful era at Manchester United but years ago there was a captain called Bryan Robson, one of the greatest players to ever play for Man Utd.

"He didn't play for teams that won leagues or European cups every year. He is still seen as one of the greatest players to play for the club. He never threw a manager or the players under the bus. He kept fighting for Man Utd.

"Watching him [Bruno] play every week, throwing his arms up at players constantly, it is a disgrace that he has called out the manager considering how he has performed this season on the pitch. Awful attitude and not what a Manchester United captain should be.

"How many managers has he had? Every single manager at Man Utd has not had an identity?

"[Como boss] Cesc Fabregas, I think he is the best young thing in managerial terms, but Man Utd is rotten from top to bottom. Everything about the club.

"This can't go on for a club of this stature. I am glad Michael Carrick came out and said that about Bruno Fernandes. That they don't run, because they don't run.

"I am delighted he brought him off and delighted he had a pop back at him."

articles.title: Arch Manning's QB1 Status Updated by Steve Sarkisian Ahead of No. 19 Texas vs. No. 7 Ole Miss
articles.summary: Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian came short Thursday of committing to Arch Manning as his starter past the No. 19 Longhorns' home game against No. 7 Ole Miss this Saturday.
articles.body:
Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian came short Thursday of committing to Arch Manning as his starter past the No. 19 Longhorns' home game against No. 7 Ole Miss this Saturday.

"It just depends," Sarkisian said about Manning's status in a Thursday Zoom call with reporters (h/t the Austin American-Statesman 's Michael Shapiro). "Every game's different.

"I think Arch has had a good week of work. He's prepared himself well, but like the team, we need to play well. So, we'll go from there."

Asked about Manning's attitude in the week leading up to the matchup, Sarkisian attributed what he described as the quarterback's edginess in part to media scrutiny of his struggles.

"At some point he's gotta fight back," Sarkisian said about media coverage of Manning, per Shapiro . "The best way to fight back is playing good football with his teammates and enjoying playing good football with his teammates."

Sarkisian also praised backup quarterback KJ Lacey ahead of Saturday's matchup.

"KJ's a good player. He's dynamic with the ball in his hands. He's a natural passer," Sarkisian said, according to Inside Texas' Evan Vieth .

Sarkisian added there were some "growing pains" in getting Lacey adjusted given his lack of prior playing time but that the four-star 2025 recruit was "coachable" and had "good rapport with his teammates," per Vieth.

The latest comments from the Longhorns coach came after he said Monday that Texas would be sticking with their incumbent starter, but that he needed to see "a better version of Arch Manning" going forward (h/t OnTexas' CJ Vogel ).

Sarkisian also said Monday that Lacey has been taking weekly first-team reps, per Vogel.

Texas was ranked as the AP Poll's top team before conceding consecutive losses to Oklahoma and Florida. Manning's decision-making has repeatedly come into question over that stretch, which was capped off last Saturday by his costly fumble late in the fourth quarter against Florida.

Manning, 22, has struggled with consistency throughout his second full season as Texas' starting quarterback.

Whether he is able to show any progress in this weekend's matchup against Ole Miss could impact whether Sarkisian continues working on his development or considers turning to Lacey down the stretch of the season.

articles.title: Celtic fans issued travel warning ahead of Celta Vigo Europa League clash
articles.summary: Celtic supporters travelling to Thursday night’s Europa League clash against Celta Vigo have been warned of potential traffic disruption near Parkhead.Celtic...
articles.body:
Celtic supporters travelling to Thursday night's Europa League clash against Celta Vigo have been warned of potential traffic disruption near Parkhead.

Fans driving to the stadium could face delays in the Shawfield area of Glasgow, where emergency Scottish Water repairs have resulted in temporary traffic lights being installed.

The disruption is affecting the junction of Shawfield Drive and Shawfield Road, with traffic management measures expected to remain in place until 7pm on Monday, October 26.

Restrictions were initially expected to ease by Wednesday evening, although subsequent updates indicate that the temporary signals will remain in operation throughout Thursday's European fixture.

Supporters travelling through the area are therefore advised to allow additional time for their journeys or consider alternative routes to Celtic Park.

The warning comes ahead of another important European night for Martin O'Neill's side, who are searching for their first Europa League points of the campaign.

Having suffered successive defeats against Ferencvaros and Benfica, Celtic will be desperate to get their European campaign back on track against the Spanish opposition.

The Hoops head into the encounter following Sunday's emphatic 7-1 victory over Hearts, with O'Neill hoping his players can carry that attacking momentum into tonight's showdown.

articles.title: Bayern Munich confirm Luis Diaz hamstring injury following Arsenal draw
articles.summary: Bayern Munich have confirmed that winger Luis Diaz sustained a hamstring injury during Wednesday’s 2-2 Champions League draw against Arsenal at the Allianz A...
articles.body:
Bayern Munich have confirmed that winger Luis Diaz sustained a hamstring injury during Wednesday's 2-2 Champions League draw against Arsenal at the Allianz Arena.

The Bundesliga champions announced on Thursday that medical examinations revealed a minor muscle fibre tear in the Colombian international's left hamstring.

Diaz, 29, will consequently be unavailable for an unspecified period, handing Bayern another injury concern during a demanding run of fixtures.

The club's official statement read: "Luis Díaz picked up a minor muscle fibre tear in his left hamstring during FC Bayern's Champions League game against Arsenal on Wednesday night."

Bayern added that the injury had been confirmed by their medical department and that the attacker would be sidelined for the foreseeable future.

No specific recovery timeline has been provided, leaving his availability for the club's upcoming domestic and European matches uncertain.

Diaz featured against Arsenal as Bayern surrendered a second-half advantage to settle for a point in an entertaining encounter.

Eberechi Eze had initially put the visitors ahead before Alphonso Davies equalised following an excellent pass from Harry Kane.

Kane subsequently converted a penalty after Jurrien Timber handled his goalbound effort, putting Bayern on course for victory.

Diaz was introduced during the second half and almost extended the hosts' lead, forcing David Raya into a save with a curling effort.

However, Declan Rice struck late following an exchange with Viktor Gyokeres to secure a draw for Arsenal.

The result extended Bayern's unbeaten home record in Champions League group-stage and league-phase matches to 40 games.

Diaz's injury now creates an additional selection problem for Bayern as they attempt to maintain their domestic momentum and improve their European results.

The Colombian has become an important attacking option since arriving from Liverpool, offering pace, direct running and versatility across the forward line.

His absence could require Bayern to adjust their attacking rotation, particularly with several important fixtures approaching.

The German champions have already experienced personnel difficulties this season, making the timing of another injury particularly unwelcome.

However, the club's description of the damage as a minor muscle fibre tear offers some encouragement regarding the potential length of his absence.

Bayern have not indicated whether Diaz will require further treatment beyond the rehabilitation programme overseen by their medical staff.

His return will therefore depend on his response to recovery work and subsequent fitness assessments.

For now, Bayern must prepare for their upcoming matches without the Colombian while awaiting further clarity on when he can resume training.
